topic.title: We check the biryani reviews, not the 'SEBI-registered' man
topic.claim: We will read 400 reviews before ordering a mixer-grinder, then hand a stranger crores because he said the words 'SEBI registered'.
topic.behaviour: A Jodhpur FIR described in a thread alleges a man claiming to be SEBI-registered got nearly ₹7 crore for options trading, with a 20% commission on gains promised. The victim, the poster's father, lost ₹1.34 crore. Many families have an older relative who trades or is being 'guided' by someone with a confident voice.
topic.mechanism: Jargon and a claimed registration work as trust shortcuts. Options trading feels like a secret that only insiders can access, and fear of missing out beats the boring step of checking a registration. Shame then keeps families from telling anyone until it's too late.
topic.group: adult children of investing parents, and first-time retail investors
real_details: The thread says an FIR was registered at a Jodhpur police station
The accused allegedly claimed to be SEBI-registered
Nearly ₹7 crore was allegedly handed over for options trading
The promise was a 20% commission on gains
The father ended up losing ₹1.34 crore
topic.why_now: A top-of-month personal finance thread shows how this scam works in practice.

score.why: Sharp, funny contrast on trust and money, same register as the QR-sticker and mutual-fund takes he's kept before.
